final_codebook.domain: Subtraction of fractions, mixed numbers, and whole numbers with simplification

skills.name: Normalize given form
skills.definition: Rewrite a nonstandard mixed number or a whole number into a subtraction-ready form, such as converting an improper fractional part into a standard mixed number or expressing a whole number as a whole plus 0 over a needed denominator.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a mixed number with an improper fractional part is rewritten as an equivalent standard mixed number.
Tag when a whole number is rewritten as a whole plus 0/d to align with fraction or mixed-number subtraction.
Tag when the rewrite is done before subtraction to make whole and fractional parts explicit.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when the step only finds a common denominator or converts to equivalent fractions.
Do not tag when the step borrows 1 from the whole part during subtraction.
Do not tag when the step only combines already computed parts into a final answer.

skills.name: Common denominator conversion
skills.definition: Find a common denominator and rewrite one or both fractions as equivalent fractions with that denominator before subtraction.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step explicitly finds an LCD or common denominator.
Tag when a step converts one or both fractions to equivalent fractions with a shared denominator.
Tag even if the common denominator equals the original denominator and the fractions remain numerically unchanged, as long as the setup is explicitly shown.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when denominators are already the same and no conversion step is shown.
Do not tag when the step only subtracts after denominators already match.
Do not tag when the step only simplifies the result.

skills.name: Subtract fraction parts
skills.definition: Subtract fractional quantities once they are in compatible form, including same-denominator fraction subtraction and the fractional part of mixed-number subtraction.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when numerators are subtracted over a common denominator.
Tag when the fractional parts of mixed numbers are subtracted after any needed setup.
Tag whether the fractional result is positive, zero, or initially negative.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when the step is only finding a common denominator or converting equivalent fractions.
Do not tag when the step only subtracts whole-number parts.
Do not tag when the step only simplifies a resulting fraction.

skills.name: Subtract whole parts
skills.definition: Subtract the whole-number components in a mixed-number or whole-number subtraction setup.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step explicitly computes the whole-part difference.
Tag when a whole number is compared with the whole part of a mixed number.
Tag when the whole-part subtraction is shown separately, even if later borrowing changes the result.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag for pure fraction items with no whole-number component.
Do not tag when the step only rewrites a whole number as a whole plus 0/d.
Do not tag when the step only combines final whole and fractional results.

skills.name: Borrow across mixed number
skills.definition: Regroup by taking 1 from the whole-number part and converting it into denominator-sized fractional units when the fractional subtraction would otherwise be negative.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step explicitly borrows 1 from the whole part.
Tag when the borrowed whole is rewritten as d/d and added to the existing fractional part.
Tag when regrouping is used to resolve a negative fractional difference in a mixed-number or whole-minus-fraction problem.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when no regrouping is needed.
Do not tag when a step only normalizes an improper mixed number or rewrites a whole as 0/d before subtraction.
Do not tag when the step only simplifies or combines the final result.

skills.name: Simplify and combine
skills.definition: Reduce the computed result to lowest terms and express it in an appropriate final form such as a fraction, mixed number, whole number, or zero.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a fraction is simplified to lowest terms.
Tag when whole and fractional results are combined into a final mixed number, whole number, fraction, or zero.
Tag when a zero fraction is rewritten as 0 or omitted from the final form.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when the step only performs subtraction without final-form rewriting.
Do not tag common-denominator conversion, normalization, or borrowing steps.
Do not tag classification statements such as problem types.

decisions.reasoning: All three experts agreed on a broader normalization/preparation concept, while only one expert isolated rewriting a whole as 0/d. These two actions are not independently robust in this item set and serve the same preparatory function, so merging improves minimality and clarity.
This skill had 3/3 consensus, appears across many items, and is clearly distinct from subtraction itself. It is independently testable and important for diagnostic resolution.

Although one expert used a broader subtraction skill, the dossiers show many items where fraction-part subtraction can be observed separately from whole-part subtraction. Keeping it separate preserves independence and better explains solution steps.

Whole-part subtraction is a distinct cognitive operation from fraction-part subtraction, with clear item evidence and separable tagging opportunities. Retaining it improves completeness and identifiability.

decisions.details: Removed C06 as a standalone skill
decisions.reasoning: C06 is a broader umbrella that collapses C04 and C05. Because fraction-part subtraction and whole-part subtraction are independently testable in the dossiers, merging them would reduce diagnostic precision and violate non-redundancy.
This skill had 3/3 consensus and represents a distinct regrouping process that is neither normalization nor subtraction. It is essential for mixed-number subtraction items requiring borrowing.

The experts agreed strongly on simplification/final-form expression, but examples showed both reduction and recombination. The final definition explicitly includes both while excluding earlier arithmetic steps for clearer annotation boundaries.

summary: The final codebook consolidates the three expert schemes into 6 skills by preserving all high-consensus operations and resolving the two main disagreements through principled merging and separation. Preprocessing actions were merged into one normalization skill, while the broader subtraction candidate was removed in favor of separate whole-part and fraction-part subtraction skills to maintain diagnostic precision. The result is a complete, minimal, and clearly bounded codebook for fraction and mixed-number subtraction.
